calls.reason: The Reuters Institute survey shows mostly infrequent ChatGPT use. Microsoft, reporting on itself for an earlier quarter, cites 1.8M paid Copilot subscribers. 'Killer app' has no threshold, so the evidence is mixed.
'Can never be solved' is an open-ended forecast. The 2026 Princeton preprint finds only small reliability gains, but it is neither an impossibility result nor a counterexample.

Two controlled studies from before the post, Wu et al. on counterfactual tasks and Lewis & Mitchell on analogies, show large drops on altered familiar tasks. GSM1k found frontier models held steady but does not undo that pattern.

AlphaEvolve shows a verifier-based hybrid with gains, but only DeepMind reports them and it builds on the earlier FunSearch. The claim was framed as a renaissance after gen AI collapses, and the evidence shows no such collapse.
WildHallucinations (July 2024) tested 15 contemporary LLMs, including GPT-4o, and found consistent factual hallucinations that retrieval did not eliminate.
